title: Two Things at Once
label: ch:ur-two-things-at-once
canDo: I can put two nouns in one sentence with اور, offer a choice with یا, turn a clause against the one before it with لیکن, and agree with somebody using ٹھیک ہے.

payoff.summary: The chapter-15 practice line bārish, dhūp, aur hawā -- which asked the learner to say a word the book had never taught -- is said with every word owned, then re-joined as a choice and refused twice over.
payoff.note: The three joiners come from three sources -- اور inherited, یا from Persian, لیکن from Arabic -- which is the whole shape of Urdu's vocabulary in one chapter.
